Principal component analysis with tidy results and optional plotting

Source: R/fs_pca.R
fs_pca.Rd

Runs a principal component analysis (PCA) on the numeric columns of data and returns loadings, scores, and the share of variance each retained component explains. PCA finds the directions of greatest spread in the data; use it to see how much of that spread a few components carry and which columns drive them.

Usage

fs_pca(
  data,
  num_pc = NULL,
  scale_data = TRUE,
  center_data = TRUE,
  label_col = NULL,
  plot = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table with at least two rows and at least one numeric column. Column names must be unique and non-empty. A non-numeric (label) column named like a retained score column (PC1, PC2, ...) would be hidden by the scores in pca_df, so that is an error. Columns in extreme units (beyond about 1e154 or below 1e-154) are kept, because the zero-variance check is relative to each column's magnitude; with scale_data = FALSE their variance cannot be represented and they are an error.

num_pc

Number of principal components to retain: a whole number >= 1, or NULL (the default) for min(2, max_possible). max_possible is min(nrow - 1, ncol) of the usable numeric data, after incomplete rows and zero-variance columns are dropped. A larger explicit value is an error.

scale_data

Logical; scale numeric columns to unit variance. Default TRUE. scale_data = TRUE with center_data = FALSE is an error, because stats::prcomp() and bigstatsr::big_scale() handle uncentered scaling differently (the latter ignores it), and the result would depend on which engine the data size selected.

center_data

Logical; center numeric columns. Default TRUE.

label_col

Optional single string naming a column of data used to label and color points. It is left out of the PCA features and carried into pca_df. Default NULL: no labels, and therefore no plot.

plot

Logical; if TRUE, print the PC1 vs PC2 scatterplot. Default FALSE, whether or not label_col is supplied. The plot object is returned in $plot either way whenever one can be built (see Details).

verbose

Logical; print progress messages naming the non-numeric columns held back as labels, the engine chosen, and any fallback from 'bigstatsr'. Default FALSE.

Value

A plain list, not an fs_result: fs_pca() reduces dimensions rather than selecting features, so it has no selected set to report. The components are:

  • pc_loadings: numeric matrix of variable loadings, one row per retained numeric feature (named) and one column per retained component (PC1, PC2, ...).

  • pc_scores: numeric matrix of observation scores, one row per kept observation and one column per retained component.

  • var_explained: numeric vector of length num_pc, the proportion of total variance carried by each retained component (see Details).

  • pca_df: data.table of the scores with the label columns (every non-numeric column, plus label_col) bound alongside, restricted to the kept rows.

  • meta: list with numeric_cols (the features actually decomposed), rows_kept (logical vector over the rows of data), n_rows_used, and n_cols_used.

  • plot: the ggplot object, present only when a plot could be built (a label_col was supplied, at least two components were retained, and 'ggplot2' is installed). Test for it with "plot" %in% names(res).

Details

PCA is unsupervised dimensionality reduction, not feature selection. Every component is a linear combination of all the retained numeric columns, chosen without reference to any outcome. A PCA therefore does not shorten the list of variables you have to measure, and the leading components are the highest-variance directions, which need not be the ones related to a response.

Before the decomposition:

  • Non-numeric columns (character, factor, logical, Date, ...) are left out of the features and carried along as labels. An explicit label_col, numeric or not, is also left out of the features.

  • Rows with a missing value in any numeric feature column are dropped. An infinite value in a feature column is an error.

  • Zero-variance columns are dropped with a warning. A column counts as zero-variance when its standard deviation is at most 1000 * .Machine$double.eps (about 2e-13) times its largest absolute value. A column that is constant up to floating-point round-off is therefore dropped, while small-unit or large-offset columns (timestamps, say) are kept.

Data with fewer than 1e7 cells is decomposed with stats::prcomp(). From 1e7 cells up, if the suggested package 'bigstatsr' is installed, bigstatsr::big_SVD() runs on a temporary file-backed matrix (the backing file is deleted when the call returns) and can compute at most one fewer component than there are usable columns. Without 'bigstatsr' the call falls back to prcomp(), and says so only when verbose = TRUE.

var_explained is the proportion of total variance explained by each retained component under both engines. It sums to 1 only when every available component is retained; with the default two components it sums to the fraction those two capture. prcomp() computes every component, so the total is the sum of all eigenvalues. big_SVD() computes only the top num_pc singular values, so the total is recovered separately from the column statistics of the (implicitly centered and scaled) matrix. Under either engine, read the entries as shares of the whole, never as shares of the components that happened to be computed.

plot controls printing only, never construction. Whenever a plot can be built (a label_col was supplied, at least two components were retained, and the suggested package 'ggplot2' is installed), the ggplot object is returned in $plot, whatever the value of plot. plot = TRUE also prints it and makes 'ggplot2' required: its absence is then an error rather than a missing $plot. plot = TRUE without a label_col, or with fewer than two retained components, warns and skips the plot.

See also

The Dimensionality reduction guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

res <- fs_pca(mtcars, num_pc = 2, label_col = "cyl")
res$var_explained
#> [1] 0.5697822 0.2644102
head(res$pca_df)
#>            PC1        PC2   cyl
#>          <num>      <num> <num>
#> 1: -0.68400200 -1.6918186     6
#> 2: -0.64964186 -1.5108421     6
#> 3: -2.45446503  0.1707165     4
#> 4: -0.25539550  2.3333568     6
#> 5:  1.68827810  0.7361403     8
#> 6:  0.02536833  2.7401361     6

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # plot = FALSE (the default) draws nothing, but $plot is built anyway
  res <- fs_pca(iris, label_col = "Species", verbose = TRUE)
  print(inherits(res$plot, "ggplot"))

  # plot = TRUE draws it as well
  res <- fs_pca(iris, label_col = "Species", plot = TRUE)
}
#> Excluding 1 non-numeric column(s) from the PCA features (kept as label candidates): Species
#> Using prcomp for PCA computation.
#> [1] TRUE
